page: OVHcloud b3-8 is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs from the AMD EPYC processor family, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is more limited, with the Geekbench multi-core score and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block reads and writes at 62.95 GB/sec and 45.99 GB/sec respectively, while small-block cached reads are weaker. Database operations, static web serving, and software compilation benchmarks also register in the lower tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the b3-8 offers dedicated CPU resources and NVMe storage at a resource density suitable for entry-level workloads. Because it avoids shared-core CPU scheduling, it provides predictable execution for single-threaded tasks. This server is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic text processing, single-threaded applications, and small-scale development environments that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high multi-core throughput or intensive memory bandwidth.
